reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in modeling climber-problem interactions using probabilistic matrix factorization (PMF), which decomposes a sparse performance matrix Y into two lower-rank matrices U and V representing climber and problem embeddings respectively. This formulation enables capturing complex, multi-faceted skill profiles beyond scalar metrics. The dot product between climber and problem vectors provides a principled way to predict performance outcomes. Unlike logistic regression models that assign fixed coefficients per climber, PMF allows for flexible, context-dependent predictions by learning latent feature representations. The framework inherently handles missing data through probabilistic inference, making it suitable for sparse datasets typical in competitive climbing. The resulting embeddings offer interpretability through their multi-dimensional nature, revealing specialized strengths and weaknesses in climbers. This approach bridges traditional statistical modeling with modern machine learning paradigms, offering scalable solutions for high-dimensional, heterogeneous sports analytics.
